note: Large Ozark upland area along the Niangua River and Jakes Creek, five miles east of Tunas. The main campground (with the only privy) is a gravel loop with back-in spurs plus sites along a spur road, in upland oak forest off the area road from the southwest entrance (Route YY), well away from the water. Four smaller primitive camping spots elsewhere, two of them at boat ramps on the Niangua; the east side (Bluff Trail entrance) has no road link to the west side. Multi-use trails are open to horses, and an unstaffed shooting range sits on the southeast side (closed Mondays). --Claude
summary: Confirmed: 50-site main campground with the only privy, FCFS, free, Rule 140 standard; free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights/50 sites/vault toilet now manual. PIN is on a minor boat-ramp camp: move ~3.1 km to the main campground (GIS 64). Waterfront riverview -> not waterfront (main camp is upland, ~1.4 km+ from the river). Phone (417) 895-6880 added (flag).
flags: INCLUSION: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Designated Camping Sites, Individual Campsites'; 'Visitors will find five primitive camping areas. The main campground has 50 sites and is the only location of a privy. No other facilities are provided in any other camping areas. Camping is all on a first come-first served basis with no permit or reservation required.' Brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted in spots designated on the area map.' Rule 140 standard, no special-use-permit-only rule, no Rule 101. Imagery of the main campground: a gravel loop with back-in spurs and more sites along a gravel spur road, a building (privy) at the loop head - drive-in, room for a 23-ft rig. The stored '~26 sites fit trailers' has no MDC source; MDC says 50 sites.

PIN (move ~3.1 km): stored 37.8629,-92.8978 is in woods beside the Niangua River boat-ramp loop on the east side (GIS 26 lot 3236, 34 m; GIS 27 camping point 65, 72 m east) - a minor camping spot. The main campground (map: the camping symbol beside the area's only privy) is GIS 27 point 64 = lot 1254, 37.85034,-92.92914, on the west side. Move the pin to 37.8504,-92.9291 (the loop junction, visible on imagery). Brochure/page: 'There is no vehicle access to the west side of area from the east side' - the main campground is reached from the southwest entrance (From Plad, Highway 64 west, Route T north, Route YY east 0.5 mile).

WATERFRONT (stored riverview -> not waterfront, downgrade): the main campground sits in upland forest on a ridge; a 1.4 km frame shows no water, and on the MDC map the nearest water (the Niangua by the north boat-ramp camp, GIS 66) is about 1.4 km away. The stored riverview evidence was only a commit reference. The minor ramp camp at the stored pin (lot 3236) is ~40 m from the Niangua (~60 m wide) across the boat-ramp loop: a ramp lot is not an open apron, so riverview at most there.

CLUSTERS (no split proposed): five GIS camping points - 64 main (50 sites, privy, west side), 66 at the north non-concrete ramp on the Niangua (1.6 km NE of main), 65 at the concrete ramp on the east side (3.1 km, own entrance off Bluff Trail), 67 south (2.0 km S) and 370 southeast near the shooting range (4.3 km). Apart from the main campground each is a single small lot or ramp spot, so none qualifies for a split. near.py: no other entry within 3 km of either point.

HORSES: no horse camp; multi-use trails open to horses ('Horses must stay on roads open to vehicular traffic or on multi-use trails posted as open to horses'), closed to horses during firearms deer season and spring turkey shooting hours.
